annotation.evidence_span: A TCP MAY implement PUSH flags on SEND calls (MAY-15).
annotation.interpretation_a: A TCP implementation is allowed to support PUSH flags on SEND calls, which could result in the PSH bit being set in the TCP header to indicate that the data should be pushed to the receiving application immediately.
annotation.interpretation_b: A TCP implementation is allowed to ignore PUSH flags on SEND calls, and instead rely on other mechanisms (e.g., buffering and setting the PSH bit in the last segment) to manage data delivery, as described in the next clause.
annotation.justification: The clause introduces an optional feature (PUSH flags on SEND calls) without fully constraining the behavior when the feature is not implemented. While the next clause provides some guidance for the case where PUSH flags are not implemented, the lack of a clear, mandatory fallback mechanism in the target clause itself introduces ambiguity in how implementations should behave in the absence of PUSH flag support.
annotation.missing_information: The clause does not specify the behavior of the TCP implementation when PUSH flags are not implemented, beyond the general 'MAY' statement. This leaves room for different implementations to handle the absence of PUSH flags in different ways, potentially leading to inconsistent behavior.
